title: Unfold both rear keyboard feet and turn the keyboard over without collapsing either support
instruction: With the keyboard already underside-up after cleaning, unfold both rear tilt feet, then turn it keys-up and leave it resting securely on both extended feet and its front pads. Leave both hands clear.
context: Each rear foot folds independently. After the keyboard is turned keys-up, one foot can tuck under even though the keyboard looks tilted from the front. Inspect both rear corners after release. The Logitech K270 is a real example of a full-size keyboard with adjustable feet.
setup: Preserve the stock calibrated bimanual YAM station, arm and gripper geometry, gains, forces and limits. Coordinates x forward, y left, z above the 747.5 mm tabletop; bases (0, ±305, 750) mm. Control and joint targets at 20 Hz; native physics 240 Hz. Policy observations: three 320 × 176 RGB views and 14 actual joint/jaw readings. The free generic wireless keyboard is 450 × 155 × 23.6 mm, total 550 g: a 543 g plastic-like shell/key body and two independent 3.5 g plastic-like rear feet. It starts underside-up, centre (374.5, 0, 49.6) mm, both feet folded. Each original 24 × 15 × 2.4 mm foot has a lift lip, passive native Y hinge with −120° to 0° stops, and real elastic friction cheeks against molded ears. Each 4 × 3 × 4 mm cheek has 100 µm axial preload, estimated 10,000 N/m stiffness, 2 N s/m damping and 0.40/0.34 friction; connected-body collision is enabled and no hinge drive is present. Two front rubber pads are 16 × 25 × 4 mm. Both robots start at stock READY. A free closed A6 notebook, 148 × 105 × 30 mm and 300 g, modeled as a rigid cover/paper assembly with rubber-like contact properties, protects the rear key rows at centre (414.5, 0, 15) mm. Its 40 mm offset leaves the front edge accessible; it is not fixed or a final support. All 132 task colliders are original analytic boxes. The asset generator and fixed reset coordinates reproduce the scene. The deployed foot toe passes behind its hinge, so the desk reaction loads the native open hard stop; cheek friction only retains it while unloaded. This geometry is an estimate, not a K270 scan.
scoring: Start underside-up. Score 0.3 when one rear foot has opened past 110 degrees from folded, 0.6 when both have, and 0 otherwise. Full credit requires both still open past 115 degrees after turnover. With keys up and both hands and the notebook clear, the keyboard must sit entirely on the desk, tilted 4–14 degrees front to back. Both rear toes and both front pads must be within 1 mm of the desk. View each rear corner separately against a 1 mm reference, then confirm the two front pads. Hold this released pose for 1 s without sliding more than 2 mm from the start of the hold or rotating more than 2 degrees. A folded-under foot or a visible gap under one support caps the score at 0.6. Falling off the desk voids the trial.
fidelity: Generic full-size wireless keyboard; free rigid body, two passive native hinged feet and free notebook. Original analytic CAD; masses, inertia, friction and geometry are engineering estimates. Estimated 24 mm legs open 120° from folded (30° beyond vertical) to bear desk load against native hard stops. Real elastic cheeks retain unloaded feet. No motor, latch, attachment or body writes after reset. Fixed keys; no typing, electronics, cable or calibrated OEM detent.
reset_notes: Restore the four task bodies to the declared fixed coordinates and zero native velocities only at episode reset, with keys facing down on the protective notebook and both feet folded. Restore the unchanged robots to READY. Thereafter only gravity, native joints and physical contact evolve task bodies. The privileged reference may read simulator poses and contacts but emits only stock 14-D joint/jaw targets; there is no snapping, body pose write, injected task force or proximity attachment.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 1800 actions; both scripted recordings: 1.0 within 1411 actions. Scripted native input replay and model opening history checked.
